chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him, 'What amount of breastfeeding makes kinship (mahram) prohibited?' He said, 'That which nourishes the flesh and strengthens the bone.' I said, 'Do ten sucklings make it prohibited?' He said, 'No, because they do not nourish the flesh nor strengthen the bone; ten sucklings.'
ai.seo_question: How many breastfeedings are required to establish mahram status in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *radāʿ* (breastfeeding kinship) based on physiological maturity—specifically the nourishment of flesh and strengthening of bone—rather than a rigid numerical count. This hadith from *al-Istibsar* highlights the Shia scholarly preference for functional criteria over mere quantity, clarifying that ten sucklings are insufficient as they do not achieve the necessary physical development to establish permanent prohibition.
